items.title: Seven members of Iran's women's football team have sought asylum, ABC understands
items.description: Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke, who was at the airport ahead of the team's departure, says border force officials made multiple representations to the players before they were due to depart Sydney.

items.title: What you need to know about Iran today, with Laura Tingle
items.description: The ABC's global affairs editor, Laura Tingle, is in Dubai and will provide daily updates on the Middle East war.

items.title: Live: Iran 'not seeking ceasefire' as US and Israel continue to pummel Tehran
items.description: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth says the US is hitting Iran with the "most intense" day of strikes since the war began. Follow live.

items.title: Iran hit with 'most intense' day of strikes, Hegseth says
items.description: The US has been pounding Iran with its "most intense" day of strikes since the war began, US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth says.

items.title: Asian hubs boom as Australians avoid Middle East airspace
items.description: Flights in limbo, a region at war, and thousands of dollars lost with no end in sight — Australian travellers are going to extreme lengths to keep their hopes of a European holiday alive despite the dire circumstances.

items.title: Foreign Facebook pages have been promoting One Nation. It wants them to stop
items.description: An ABC NEWS Verify investigation uncovers a raft of foreign Facebook accounts targeting Australian users. And they're just the tip of the iceberg.

items.title: Financial markets 'sleepwalking into a storm' as money trumps logic
items.description: "Up the stairs and down the elevator" has been the rule of thumb for decades in financial markets — but apparently it's not the case any longer.

items.title: Wide field of candidates emerges to replace David Littleproud
items.description: Four Nationals are emerging as contenders to lead the party, with Bridget McKenzie, Matt Canavan and Kevin Hogan declaring their candidacy.

items.title: Report says hours of unpaid work placed on First Nations people
items.description: A landmark Indigenous-led report reveals that racism remains a daily reality for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander workers and, at the current rate of change, "it will take 118 years to eliminate racial slurs from Australian workplaces".

items.title: Evidence shows just how broken the NSW mental healthcare system is
items.description: An alleged murder by a man who absconded from Cumberland Hospital shines a spotlight on a NSW mental healthcare system that may be more broken than first thought.

items.title: This outdated medical practice 'reflects very low respect for women'
items.description: Outdated medical devices are being used to perform a common obstetrics procedure on Australian women that can cause a condition known as Asherman's syndrome.

items.title: Australia's fuel supply struggles grind some businesses to a halt
items.description: Dozens of fishing trawlers have been stranded as a result of Australia's worsening fuel shortages, which some have described as the worst they have ever seen.

items.title: Live: Roads cut off, homes without power as Bundaberg flood peak approaches
items.description: Bundaberg is facing its worst flood in more than a decade, with the Burnett River projected to peak at 7.6 metres this morning.

items.title: After a scammer stole her life savings, Claudia took on her bank and won
items.description: Claudia Lee's ING savings account was drained by a scammer while she was travelling overseas — but it took 18 months before the bank was forced to take responsibility.

items.title: Two new novels lift the curtain on what life is really like as a royal
items.description: With Queen Mary of Denmark soon to arrive in Australia and scandal engulfing the House of Windsor, royals are swamping our news cycle. So why are readers so fascinated by royal fiction?

items.title: Kurt Cobain's Smells Like Teen Spirit guitar could fetch up to $7m at auction
items.description: The iconic six-string that gave a sound to an era's angst is among a treasure trove of items set to be sold at a New York auction.

items.title: Quiz: Can you find your way around the world?
items.description: Where would you find the Frank Lloyd Wright marvel, Fallingwater? And what's the capital of Fiji?

items.title: Bundaberg residents brace as floodwater from Burnett River expected to peak this morning
items.description: The Bureau of Meteorology says rain will ease for most of Queensland today but major flooding could last for days.

items.title: Lululemon fined $700,000 over hundreds of thousands of spam emails
items.description: The Australian Communications and Media Authority says activewear fashion brand Lululemon sent more than 370,000 emails containing marketing content without an unsubscribe option.

items.title: The 86yo who spent his working life protecting world leaders
items.description: The family of a former NSW Police detective says while his job was to ensure the safety of foreign leaders, at home he was just Dad.

items.title: Digital harassment, child abuse material common federal crimes in Vic
items.description: Digital crimes involving harassment, or distributing child abuse material, are among the most common federal crimes being sentenced in Victoria, a new report shows.

items.title: 'Jackie told me she was hurt': Sandilands responds to radio drama
items.description: In his first statement since he was ordered off the air after a blow-up with co-host Jackie "O" Henderson, Sandilands calls on ARN Media, owner of KIIS FM, to "honour our agreement" and let him return to the Kyle and Jackie O Show.

items.title: What is behind the Greek yoghurt shortage hitting supermarkets?
items.description: Greek yoghurt has been flying off the shelves as viral social media trends spruik its high-protein benefits.

items.title: Star Hawk regrets 'foolish mistake' that landed him in US jail
items.description: Dylan Moore opens up on an off-season incident involving a scissor-lift that cost him his Hawthorn vice-captaincy.

items.title: Lions' defensive stocks cop major blow after unsuccessful tribunal date
items.description: Brisbane must tackle a red-hot Sydney side without two of its most important defenders after the AFL tribunal upheld bans handed to Harris Andrews and Darcy Gardiner.
